rows.grounds: compound describing tvām; barhiḥ-mukha (fire-mouthed, Agni) taken as one's own mouth by the worshippers
locative plural indicating the ritual setting
compound; followers or people of that group/tradition
dative of purpose indicating repose or final rest

items.question: How do certain sacrificial worshippers find repose in the deity through identification with the fire-mouthed one?
premises: Some people belonging to a particular tradition approach the deity in sacrifices.
They apprehend the deity as having the fire-mouthed one as their own mouth.
This apprehension serves as the means for their repose.
items.inference: Therefore, for these sacrificial worshippers, the deity is the locus of rest when recognized through the form of the fire-mouthed sacrificial principle.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tat in tat+janāḥ is context-dependent and not fully explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: In sacrifices, some of their people seek you for rest, taking the fire-mouthed one as their own mouth.
